Step 2: Apply for 
Instructor Designation

The Parent/Instructor will submit an application to become the 
instructor. The fee to apply is $20.00 and a separate application 
must be submitted for each child you will 
be teaching. https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/
ParentTaught/PTSelect.aspx
Step 3: Read the 
Parent Taught  
Program Guide
After the Instructor Designation Services 
application is processed, the Parent Taught 
Program Guide will be emailed to you.Step 4: Research, 
Select, & Purchase a 
Parent Taught Course
Driver Education Provider Search.
Step 5: You are  
now ready to begin 
Parent Taught
Step 6: Obtaining a Learner 
License Certificate of  
Completion
Most parent taught 
providers will issue 
the Learner License Certificate of Completion once the student has completed Module One. 
Some providers will issue the Learner License Certificate of Completion when the student 
completes the full 24 hours of classroom phase.
Step 7: Schedule an appointment with  
Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)
Students must take the Learner License 
Certificate of Completion to DPS 
along with a high school diploma, its 
equivalent (GED) or completed  
Verification of Enrollment and 
Attendance (VOE) form. Check DPS 
website for the full list of required 
documents: Texas Learners License as 
a Teen. Students must have a Learner 
License before they may begin any  
behind-the-wheel training.
Step 8: Complete  
remaining classroom phase 
and in-car training
Students will  
complete the 
remaining portion 
of the course and 
will receive a 
Driver License  
Certificate of  
Completion upon  
successful completion.  
In addition to the 24 hours of classroom, 7 hours of observation, and 7 hours of behind the wheel, students must 
complete 30 additional hours of in-car training including at least 10 hours of nighttime practice, in the presence of a 
person at least 21 years of age, has at least one year of driving experience, and holds a valid driver license.
Step 9: Complete the Impact 
Teens Driver Program (ITTD)
The ITTD program is 
a DPS course created 
to educate drivers 
about the risks and 
consequences of 
distracted driving, 
ultimately saving lives. 
The course must be 
completed within 90 days of 
taking the driving test.
Step 10: Schedule Second  
Appointment with DPS
Students must take the Driver License 
Certificate of Completion to DPS along 
with the ITTD Program Certificate. 
Check DPS website for the full list of 
required documents Texas Provisional 
License as a Teen. Step 11: Congratulations, 
you are ready to drive!
Students will be issued a Provisional License that allows students to drive independently  
with some restrictions. Those restrictions are: Passengers—May not drive with more than one passenger in the 
vehicle under 21 who is not a family member. Curfew—Driving is restricted between midnight and 5 a.m. unless for 
work, school activities, or emergencies. No cell phones allowed—All cell phone use is prohibited, including hands-
free devices unless it’s an emergency.
Step 12: Driver License
This Provisional License 
expires on the student’s 
18th birthday. After 
turning 18, the student 
must renew the license 
to receive a regular 
driver license without 
restrictions.
